about: Live non-regression of the four root-cause fixes of the 2026-09-19 plan.
Everything this file creates lives under ${SANDBOX} and nowhere else. The campaign's
namespace, user, group and systemd unit are NOT recreated: none of the four fixes touch them.
Teardown is `rm -r --`, never `rm -rf`: `rm\s+-rf` is the first blacklist pattern, so `rm -rf`
is refused with exit 4 and the directory would stay while the run looked clean.
WHAT ACTUALLY STANDS BETWEEN A CASE AND THE HOST. Not run.py: it has no guard() and never had
one on this branch (`grep -c 'def guard' scripts/live_probe/run.py` -> 0). The plan text that
dispatched this file claimed otherwise, and a safety rule citing an absent mechanism is worse
than no rule. The real protection is entirely SERVER-SIDE, and both halves were observed firing:
- the destructive-confirmation gate: `Command denied: ssh_exec is annotated destructive and
stdin is not a terminal, so there is nobody to confirm with` -> exit 4. run.py passes
stdin=DEVNULL, so a destructive case without `yes: true` is refused, never prompted.
- the config blacklist: `Command matches blacklist pattern: ...` -> refused before any SSH
traffic. Note the ORDER: the gate runs BEFORE the blacklist, so a blacklisted destructive
command is confirmed and then refused anyway (fails closed).
A case is therefore only as safe as what it asks for. Write it as if nothing would stop it.
RUN IT IN THREE PHASES, NEVER IN ONE SHOT. run.py dispatches every case of a run through one
ThreadPoolExecutor, so ordered cases must not share a run: with --jobs 2 the setup, the write
cases and the teardown race each other. `--report` only CHOOSES the path: run.py:205 writes a
report either way, and its default lands under the gitignored `.superpowers/probes/`, where the
artefact exists and is condemned. Point it here instead. Committed artefacts, three full passes:
report-pass1-{A,B,C,C2}.json  the run every verdict in the task report is quoted from
report-pass2-{A,B,C,C2}.json  re-run after the last edits to this file
report-pass3-{A,B,C,C2}.json  produced by the commands below exactly as written
report-pass4-B.json           H07/H07b alone, re-run after ruling R32 set the opt-out
Passes 1 and 2 predate the --baseline/owner split and the `error=` needles, so their JSON shows
`baseline: false`. Do not look for `owner` there: run.py:208 writes only binary, host, baseline
and results, so a case's owner lives in THIS file and nowhere else. The per-case `ok` flags are
identical across all three passes. The `report-*.json` name is load-bearing: typos.toml excludes
that glob, because run.py stores each case's output truncated at out[:400] and the cut lands
mid-word.
PROVENANCE, WHICH NO REPORT JSON CARRIES. run.py:208 records only binary, host, baseline and
results, and `binary` is the bare string "./target/debug/bridge-mcp" — no revision, no
--features, no timestamp. That path is not an identity: `make ci` builds the bin target with
DEFAULT features and rewrites it, which happened once mid-campaign. What followed is the opposite
of silent, and worth stating exactly: the default-features binary could not parse this machine's
config at all ("unknown variant winrm") and refused to start — that loudness is the only reason
the swap did not yield measurements from a build nobody chose. Rebuild after every `make ci` and
re-check `validate` before measuring. run.py is not ours to change, so this is written down here.
passes 1-3   bridge-mcp 3.0.0 (rev ced947b58070), --features full,winrm,psrp. That revision is
recorded only in the task-5 report, which is gitignored; this is the first
committed statement of it, and the gap is why this paragraph exists. It does not
weaken those verdicts: `git diff ced947b c4c9f07 -- src/ Cargo.toml Cargo.lock` is
empty, so that binary is source-identical to the tip they were filed against.
pass 4       commit 741dcff18173b731fdae6533768449c8e27c019c, built with
CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 cargo build --features full,winrm,psrp --bin bridge-mcp,
reporting `3.0.0 (rev 741dcff18173-dirty)` where dirty is this file and the two
pass-4 artefacts, none of them compiled. Config: the legacy
~/.config/mcp-ssh-bridge/config.yaml, 7 hosts, 353 tools, Permissive.
H-session.py has no report JSON at all, so its stdout is committed beside these as
H-session-pass4.txt, with the same provenance header. Four earlier runs of it exist only as a
quotation inside the task report; this is the first one kept as an artefact.
python3 scripts/live_probe/run.py BIN --cases <this> --path both --jobs 2 --baseline \
--only H00   --report scripts/live_probe/campaign/2026-09-19/report-pass3-A.json
... --only H01,H01b,H03,H03b,H07,H07b --report .../report-pass3-B.json
... --only H90 --report .../report-pass3-C.json   then  --only H91 --report .../report-pass3-C2.json
No sudo case creates ${SANDBOX}: a `mkdir -p` under `sudo` would make the directory root-owned,
and /tmp is sticky, so the unprivileged teardown could then no longer remove it.
EXPECTED EXIT CODE. Nothing in this file is expected to fail any more. H07 and H07b were the
two exceptions: they assert the RIGHT answer to defect D1 and carried `owner: r20`, so WITH
--baseline they reported `KO(e)` and did not count, and WITHOUT it the run exited 2 and that 2
was the expected value. Ruling R32 then applied the opt-out StandardTool documents for exactly
this case (`NONZERO_EXIT_IS_ERROR = false` on ssh_service_status), so both now PASS and both
carry `owner: base`. Every case being `owner: base` makes --baseline INERT here: run.py:192
excuses a failure only when the owner is not `base`, so with the flag or without it any KO is
unexpected and the run exits non-zero. The flag is kept in the commands below so pass4's report
is shape-identical to pass3's (`baseline: true`) and the only difference between the two is the
verdicts. Changing an expectation invalidates every verdict obtained under the old one, so H07
and H07b were re-run against the host after the const changed, with --jobs 1 and --only H07,H07b
— report-pass4-B.json. Those two cases only: they create nothing and remove nothing, so no
sandbox phase had to run beside them.
H02, H04, H05 and H06 are NOT here and cannot be. H02 asserts on the bridge host's own audit
log, not on a tool's output. H04/H05/H06 need several tool calls inside ONE server process,
because a session lives in the SessionManager of that process and run.py spawns one process per
case (same reason mcp_probe.py exists). They run from H-session.py in this directory.
WHAT snapshot.py IN THIS TREE ACTUALLY COMPARES — the plan predicted an exit 1 on
`packages_count` and `pods`, which this version cannot produce. Its take() records 7 fields only
(pods, node_ready, failed_units, sandbox_present, k3s_active, alerts_raw, rc) and its diff()
guards 4 of them (node_ready, failed_units, sandbox_present, k3s_active) plus the pod set, which
trips past 2 changes. `packages_count`, `units_count`, `users`, `groups`, `crons`,
`listening_ports` and `k8s_workloads` exist in the archived reference snapshot, written by a
later version of the script, and are never read. Expect exit 1 from the pods alone — but only
once the churn EXCEEDS 2 (snapshot.py:51 counts `gone + new > 2`): at two or fewer changed pods
the per-pod lines still print and `--diff` exits 0, which is a correct comparison and not a
broken one. Do not loosen the flags to make it pass. Also: `sandbox_present` greps /tmp for
`bridge-campaign`, not for ${SANDBOX}, so it stays false while this sandbox exists — H91 is the
teardown proof, not it.

cases.note: Minimal sandbox. Unprivileged on purpose, so H90 can remove it.
Task 1, the report's own command. Shows the compound still runs under elevation.

Task 1, the DISCRIMINATING case. H01 alone cannot fail: the old prefix form (`sudo -n touch … && echo ok`) elevates the first process and still prints ok. Only a SECOND element that needs root separates them — prefix gives 0\n1000, the shipped wrap `sudo -n bash -c '<all>'` gives 0\n0.
Task 3. 6 = EXIT_REMOTE_FAILURE (src/cli/runner.rs), distinct from the bridge's own 1-5. `exit=` and not `error=`: run.py's `error=` needs rc != 0, which is the very thing D1 used not to deliver.

Task 3 on the MCP path: the result carries isError, which run.py reports as rc != 0. The process exit code 6 is a CLI-only contract, so `exit=6` would be wrong here. The needle is NOT optional: `error=` with an empty needle reduces to `rc != 0` (run.py:124), which a server that failed to even start also satisfies — measured, it reported OK against a binary that could not load the config.

Ruling R32, live — R20 had deferred this pending exactly this measurement. apt-daily.service is loaded and normally inactive (dead), so `systemctl status` exits 3, and Task 3's blanket rule turned that correct, read-only answer into a failure (exit 6, isError) while the audit line for the same call said Success{exit_code:3} — the product contradicting itself. StandardTool has the opt-out for exactly this ('a probe whose verdict IS the code'), and ssh_service_status now sets it: NONZERO_EXIT_IS_ERROR = false. So this case PASSES, and its owner is `base`: a KO here is a regression, not an expected red. Evidence after the change: report-pass4-B.json.

The same defect from the MCP path: isError on a status query that answered. Passes since the opt-out, and `owner: base` for the same reason as H07. This is the case that carries the fix on the path a CLI exit code cannot speak for.
Teardown proof: the sandbox is gone. Needle mandatory, same reason as H03b — a bare `error=` here would pass on any failure at all, including a binary that never reached the host.
